Optional Ready-Made Gut Stacks
I don't think there's one supplement stack (a set of supplements you take together) that heals everyone's gut, and no stack can do the phases above for you. So do those first, in order, and only go after bugs and parasites if your symptoms are still there after you've changed your diet. Then a stack can help with the rebuilding in Phase 5, once you're clear of infection and it's time to feed the good bacteria again.
That said, some people want a ready-made stack rather than buying every ingredient for it separately. So, if I were to recommend a general "repair and rebuild" approach, it would be a stack that covers three categories:
1.
First, support the Microbiome with a well-tolerated probiotic or probiotic system.
2.
Then keep the probiotics well-fed with a good prebiotic, and take butyrate itself or something that helps short-chain fatty acid production, especially the main one, butyrate.
3.
Other nutrients will help support barrier repair, such as glutamine, zinc carnosine, colostrum, mucosal-support herbs, or similar compounds.

365caa04-7e58-4640-997b-1c51efda47bd.text:
Gemini suggested these kits to me, but so far they're the best ones I've seen, tho I haven't used them myself, so check the reviews. Designs for Health GI Revive is one of the more complete gut-lining repair formulas. You still need the rest of a gut protocol with it.
 There's also Dr.
 Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit, which makes sense if leaky gut is your main problem. Microbiome Labs Total Gut Restoration is the best general stack of these, because you get mucosal support along with the probiotic and prebiotic.

Microbiome Labs Total Gut Restoration covers all three categories, with a probiotic, a prebiotic and a product for the gut lining in one kit, so it's the best general one.
 Dr. Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit has a probiotic and two lining products, one of them glutamine, but no prebiotic, so it's more for when leaky gut is your main problem.
 And Designs for Health GI Revive is only the third category, a powder of gut-lining nutrients and herbs, so you'd still need a probiotic and a prebiotic with it.

Start any kit at a low dose and build up as your gut gets used to it.
 The prebiotic part especially can give you gas at first, since that's what your bacteria make when they ferment it (resistant starch does it too), and a new probiotic can bloat you or upset your stomach for a while.

c5d802b9-5c37-485a-adb3-19b15e44bcc5.text: But don't start a stack at all before seeing a doctor if you're bleeding from your gut or losing weight fast, because supplements won't fix whatever's behind that, and the same goes for bad pain, a fever or getting dehydrated. And if you're pregnant (berberine isn't safe then), your immune system is weak (probiotics are live bacteria, and a weak immune system can't always keep them in check), or you have an IBD flare, cancer or another serious illness, work out what to take with your doctor instead of putting a stack together yourself.

b795a02c-49c8-45c7-9289-7d56d7533cd0.text:
But don't start a stack at all before seeing a doctor if you notice blood in stool (if it's blood from upper digestive tract, it could be smelly, black & tarry, not red like from lower GI). If you're losing weight fast, that's another contra-indication, because these supplements may not fix whatever's behind that, and the same goes for other emergency signs like severe pain, a fever or dehydration. And if you're pregnant, some herbs and supplements, like berberine, aren't safe.
 If your immune system is weak, some probiotics could be risky since they're live bacteria that need to be kept in check to prevent overgrowth. If you have an IBD flare, cancer or another serious illness, work out what to take with your doctor instead of putting a stack together yourself.
